problem: Object-goal VLN policies treat a stable stop as task completion and only reach category-level targets, so they often stop at a same-category distractor instead of the user's own object. BLV users cannot visually check this, so a false success is harmful.
motivation: BLV users often need one specific personal object, and having to walk the space and aim a camera themselves is burdensome. A robot can provide mobility and viewpoints, but the user must be able to trust a 'Found' report. The paper therefore separates navigation-level candidate discovery from instance-level acceptance.
key_idea: A multi-agent system where a smartphone teaches a personal object once (semantic profile plus multi-view DINOv2 reference bank), a Uni-NaVid navigator proposes stop candidates, and a verifier checks each candidate against the references, so the mission ends only on PASS and otherwise triggers recovery and continued search.
insight: Navigation stopping confidence does not imply object identity: 3 consecutive STOP outputs still gave wrong candidates (15/20 sequential first-stops were wrong; 6 Astra-only trials had wrong stable candidates). Verification plus continued search turned 12 of 15 initially wrong first candidates into successes, with the verifier rejecting 27 of 28 incorrect candidates. The cost is longer completion time (225.5 s vs 160.3 s) and dependence on a fixed similarity threshold; borderline scores caused the failures. The context (anchor) check gave no observed benefit, since all 12 checks returned MATCH, including the false acceptance.
method: Target Teaching Agent: GPT-6 Astra analyzes four guided smartphone videos (front, side, top, different background) into a profile P={category, nav instruction, movable/context-stable, optional anchor}. Grounding DINO crops are filtered by confidence, size, sharpness and clipping, encoded with DINOv2 (768-d, L2-normalized), and at most 8 diverse reference crops are kept.

Navigation Agent: Uni-NaVid takes egocentric RGB and a category+color instruction (e.g. 'black umbrella') and outputs forward/left/right/stop, mapped to Go2 velocities behind a clearance safety gate. A candidate is produced only after three consecutive all-stop outputs, and the first-stop image is sent for verification.

Verification Agent: Grounding DINO localizes the category in the candidate image (highest-confidence box). The crop is DINOv2-encoded and S = max cosine similarity to the reference bank, with PASS if S >= 0.6. A movable target below threshold is UNCERTAIN and a missing detection is REJECT. Context-stable targets also need the stored anchor detected in the same image (co-presence only).

Coordination and Recovery Agent: a deterministic controller. PASS ends the mission with Found. UNCERTAIN or REJECT triggers a predefined recovery action, clears the Uni-NaVid history, and restarts navigation with the same instruction, until PASS, a non-recoverable error, or the 600 s limit.

Accessible smartphone interface (SwiftUI): 'Teach a new item' and 'Find an item', a local object library, AR reference-point capture guidance (about 0.40 m of movement and at least 4 s in view), speech, haptics and VoiceOver. Only four states are exposed (Searching, Found, Stopped, Search failed), and Found appears only after verification.

numbers_note: Custom real-robot benchmark, not a standard one. Trial counts are small (20 and 12). The sequential baseline is reconstructed from RoboFind runs. Rows 3 and 4 are subsets of the 20 runs, except that the Astra-only trials were separate executions.
results: On 20 real-robot trials, RoboFind reaches 85.0% success against 25.0% for the reconstructed sequential first-stop baseline, and cuts false success from 75.0% to 5.0%. On six shared targets it reaches 10/12 against 5/12 for GPT-6 Astra-only. Successful missions take longer (225.5 s vs 160.3 s).
limitations: Small-scale evaluation (10 targets, 2 trials each, 6 household scenes) with no user study with BLV participants, and the sequential baseline is reconstructed rather than run independently
The fixed similarity threshold (0.6) causes borderline errors (one false accept at S=0.672, rejects of correct candidates at 0.458 and 0.507), and mission-API interruptions caused a timeout
Context/anchor check checks only co-presence, not spatial relations, and showed no measurable benefit; runtime is higher because of recovery
